correctness.rationale: The generating tetrahedron for each vertex is exactly its four-vertex open neighborhood. For n>=5, the opposite-fiber pair has its unique common graph neighbor at the center, so the first triangle/tetrahedron and then edge/triangle are actual free-face pairs. The 3n centers give 6n independent collapses. Remaining 6n triangles have 3n vertices and 9n edges, and vertex links are connected six-cycles; the oriented triangle formula cancels every edge over integers. The connected orientable closed surface has Euler characteristic zero and is a PL torus. The automorphism argument establishes noncirculant n multiples of three. The proof covers every n>=5, unlike the finite checker which checks n=5,...,14.

originality.rationale: The recent full-text complete-graph by cycle theorem specifically assumes m>=4 and states that it makes no claim for m=3. Shukla 2019 classifies degree-four circulant neighborhood complexes and consequently overlaps only the cyclic subfamily; for 3|n the graph K_3 Cartesian C_n is provably not circulant by its automorphism group S_3 x D_n, lacking an element of order 3n. The 2026 toroidal square-grid theorem requires all lattice periods Manhattan length >=5 and excludes the triangle fiber. Thus no inspected theorem implies the previously unclassified infinite 3|n subfamily. Precise local collapse extends uniformly beyond those regimes. Exact indexed queries and own historical claim search found no complete covering result; searches cannot rule out unindexed equivalences.
residual_risks: An unindexed treatment of noncirculant 4-regular triangular cylinders or a stronger general theorem might be equivalent.
Earlier Shukla methods resemble local collapses; the circulant coprime-3 subfamily is not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The m=3 boundary of a studied infinite product family changes qualitatively from the m>=4 wedge of spheres to an aspherical torus, with a nontrivial integral degree-one cup pairing and fundamental group Z^2. The noncirculant 3|n subfamily is infinite and naturally forced by the graph product arithmetic, rather than an arbitrary finite parameter choice. Uniform 6n elementary collapses and the explicit PL torus core explain this transition constructively; these are useful structural and reproducible information.
